chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi - (and he was from the Waqifiya) - he said:

I visited Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and with him was his son Abul Hasan. He said to me: 'O Ziyad, this is my son Ali. His writing is my writing, his speech is my speech, his messenger is my messenger, and whatever he says, the saying is his saying.'

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim, the kunya of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abul Hasan, the kunya of Imam Ali al-Ridha (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الوَاقِفَةِ: The Waqifiya, a sect that stopped believing in the Imamate at a specific Imam.
key_terms.رَسُولَهُ: His messenger (the specific envoy authorized to convey the Imam's orders).
key_terms.كِتَابَهُ: His writing (referring to the Imam's written correspondence or decrees).

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Kadhim's declaration regarding Ali ibn Musa's writing and speech?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* records Imam al-Kadhim’s explicit designation of Ali ibn Musa (al-Ridha) as his successor, emphasizing the continuity of divine authority through the equivalence of their writings, speech, and messengers. Notably, Ziyad ibn Marwan is identified as a *Waqqafiyya* (one who paused at the Imamate of Musa al-Kadhim), making this declaration a crucial textual proof for the immediate succession to the eighth Imam. The statement underscores the concept of *Ismah* (infallibility) and the inseparability of the Imam’s word from divine command in Shia theology.
